docs.title: MediSource AI — Hospital Procurement Intelligence Platform
docs.text: MediSource AI is an agentic, AI-powered procurement automation platform built specifically for healthcare supply chains — including hospital pharmaceuticals, surgical consumables, biomedical equipment, cold-chain vaccines, and equipment Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs).

docs.title: Why Healthcare Supply Chains?
docs.text:
Procurement in healthcare is fundamentally distinct from generic enterprise supply chains. A single supply disruption, expired drug batch, or counterfeit vendor can impact patient lives and cause severe regulatory violations:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Healthcare Domain Entities                      │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ • Vendors: Pharmaceutical distributors, biomedical contractors, PPE   │
│   suppliers vetted against drug license IDs, CDSCO/FDA, and sanctions.  │
│                                                                        │
│ • Documents: Invoices, POs, quotations, cold-chain compliance certs,   │
│   and drug batch analysis certificates.                                │
│                                                                        │
│ • Inventory: Pharmacy & ward stock with SKU, batch, and strict expiry  │
│   tracking with cold-chain integrity enforcement.                      │
│                                                                        │
│ • Contracts: Biomedical equipment AMCs, NDAs, and supply agreements    │
│   dynamically compiled from approved items with e-signatures.          │
│                                                                        │
│ • Risk: Multi-dimensional scoring (compliance, fraud, financial,       │
│   operational, spend volatility, supplier delivery SLAs).              │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.text:

docs.title: Key Highlights
docs.text:
Zero-Key Resilient Fallback

document_intelligence runs LLM extraction and fraud screening using Groq (llama3-70b-8192 or mixtral-8x7b-32768). If GROQ_API_KEY is not provided or the network is unreachable, it seamlessly falls back to a deterministic regex, keyword-matching, and mathematical consistency engine. The platform runs 100% locally out of the box!

Database-per-Service Architecture

Each microservice maintains an isolated PostgreSQL database (medisource_documents, medisource_vendors, medisource_approvals, medisource_inventory, medisource_contracts, medisource_risk). Cross-service data synchronization is mediated strictly through Kafka events.

Strict Cold-Chain & Expiry Safeguards

Pharmaceutical consumables with cold-chain requirements cannot be arbitrarily split across disparate batches. Stock reservation rejects expired or non-compliant lots automatically.

docs.title: 3. Header Specification & Gateway Propagation
docs.text:
All requests from the frontend client send the following context headers: - X-User-Role: Key of active role (e.g. department_manager) - X-User-Id: Unique identifier (e.g. usr_sarah_01) - X-User-Name: Display name (e.g. Dr. Sarah)

Nginx gateway proxies these headers upstream to all FastAPI microservices (proxy_set_header X-User-Role $http_x_user_role;, etc.).

docs.title: 4. OPA (Open Policy Agent) RBAC Rules
docs.text:
Policy location: policies/opa/rbac_rules.rego

Evaluates path, method, and role to produce decision: 

package medisource.rbac

default allow = false

Services query OPA or use internal FastAPI security dependency require_roles(...) enforcing identical policy semantics.

docs.title: Architecture Diagrams
docs.text:
Visual architectural diagrams generated from the live system are available under docs/diagrams/:

Diagram Description Artifact Approval Workflow OPA routing policy, sequential approver chains, and Temporal SLA escalation Risk Intelligence ML Layer Supervised 6-dimension regressor (17 features) + IsolationForest anomaly detector Kafka Event Layers Publisher/Subscriber relationship across domain microservices

docs.title: 1. Document Intelligence (:8001)
docs.text:
• Ingestion Pipeline: Multi-source ingestion (file upload, API, email, shared drive), computing content SHA-256 hashes to prevent duplicate processing.
  • Dual-Tier OCR & Extraction:
    • Tier 1 (LLM-First): Leverages Groq (llama3-70b-8192) to parse complex document layouts, line items, taxes, supplier details, and medical equipment serials.
    • Tier 2 (Deterministic Fallback): Runs OpenCV pre-processing + PaddleOCR with regex matching and arithmetic validation. Operates completely offline without API keys.
  • Fraud Detection Engine: Arithmetic reconciliation (sum of line items vs. total, tax anomalies, missing GSTIN) combined with semantic checks for suspicious pricing or irregular drug batch numbers.
  • Review Queue: Documents with confidence < 0.75 or flagged fraud are routed to human review (GET /documents?status=needs_review).

docs.title: 2. Vendor Intelligence (:8002)
docs.text:
• Master Data: Maintains regulatory and profile data for medical equipment vendors, pharmaceutical distributors, and biomedical contractors.
  • Healthcare Verification:
    • Validates Drug License number format and validity period.
    • Validates CDSCO/FDA registration IDs and GSTIN checksums.
    • Matches against sanctions and regulatory blacklists.
  • Vendor Resolution: Exposes GET /vendors/resolve used by document_intelligence to map extracted text strings to canonical vendor IDs via fuzzy string matching.

docs.title: 3. Approval Workflow (:8003)
docs.text:
• Policy-Driven Routing: Evaluates Open Policy Agent (approval_rules.rego) combining:
    • Purchase spend thresholds (< \$5k, \$5k–\$25k, > \$25k)
    • Requesting hospital department (Cardiology, Oncology, ICU, General)
    • Vendor dynamic risk band (low, medium, high)
  • Temporal Workflow Engine: Manages long-running workflows with automated timeout alarms and escalation:
    • Step 1: Department Manager (SLA: 24h)
    • Step 2: Finance Manager (SLA: 48h)
    • Step 3: Compliance Officer (for pharmaceuticals / cold-chain items)
    • Step 4: Procurement Director (high spend or elevated risk)
  • Concurrency Protection: Redis atomic locks prevent duplicate submissions of identical procurement orders.

docs.title: 4. Inventory Intelligence (:8004)
docs.text:
• Pharmaceutical Lot & Batch Control: Stocks tracked by SKU, lot number, warehouse aisle, and expiration date.
  • Cold-Chain Guardrails: Strictly prevents splitting refrigerated items across non-compliant batches.
  • Reservation Engine: Acquires distributed Redis locks per SKU during reservation. Automatically releases expired holds via a background reaper task.
  • Autonomous Backorders: Emits inventory.backorder events when available stock is below order quantities.

docs.title: 5. Contract Intelligence (:8005)
docs.text:
• Automated Document Generation: Jinja2 templates for standard hospital agreements:
    • Medical Equipment Supply Agreement
    • Biomedical Equipment AMC (Annual Maintenance Contract)
    • Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDA)
  • E-Signature Integration: Integrates with OpenSign via REST API (OPENSIGN_BASE_URL) for digital envelope dispatch, signature tracking, and webhook execution.
  • Lifecycle Auditing: Tracks contract versions, automated 30/60-day renewal reminders, and regulatory compliance flags.

docs.title: 6. Risk Intelligence (:8006)
docs.text:
• Supervised ML Regressor: Multi-output Gradient Boosting Regressor trained over 17 empirical features across 6 dimensions:
    • Compliance Risk
    • Fraud Risk
    • Financial Risk
    • Supplier Delivery Performance
    • Spend Volatility
    • Operational Risk
  • Unsupervised Anomaly Detection: An IsolationForest detector flags abnormal vendor behavior (sudden invoice spikes, uncharacteristic round-dollar invoices, delivery delays).
  • MLflow Model Registry: Production model artifacts and hyperparameter logs are versioned in MLflow.
  • Continuous Learning: Ingests observations from Kafka (documents.processed, procurement.request.created) to refresh vendor risk scores dynamically.

docs.title: Open Policy Agent (OPA) Integration
docs.text:
MediSource AI isolates authorization logic into declarative Rego policies located under policies/opa/:

  1. rbac_rules.rego: Enforces role permissions based on incoming HTTP path, method, and user role headers (X-User-Role).
  2. approval_rules.rego: Determines approver routing dynamically based on total spend, requesting department, and real-time vendor risk tier.

Microservices query OPA via its high-performance REST endpoint (POST http://opa:8181/v1/data/medisource/approvals).

docs.title: 1. Can I run MediSource AI without an internet connection or Groq API key?
docs.text: Yes. MediSource AI is architected with a two-tier extraction engine: - If GROQ_API_KEY is provided, the platform uses Groq LLMs (llama3-70b-8192 or mixtral-8x7b-32768) for deep semantic extraction and intelligent fraud screening. - If GROQ_API_KEY is left blank or the network is offline, the service automatically falls back to an offline rule-based pipeline (OpenCV preprocessing, PaddleOCR, regex pattern extractors, and arithmetic consistency verifications). The entire stack runs end-to-end inside Docker without any external API calls.

docs.title: 2. Why use Apache Kafka instead of direct REST calls between services?
docs.text: Healthcare procurement involves multiple cascading side-effects that should not block or fail user transactions: - When an invoice is processed, vendor_intelligence links the document, approval_workflow initiates approval tracking, and risk_intelligence updates behavioral metrics. - Using Kafka guarantees: - Service Decoupling: Services can restart or scale without cascading outages. - Idempotency: Message keys (e.g. document_id, request_id) ensure redelivery does not produce duplicate orders or double-counted spend. - Auditability: Every supply chain state transition is preserved in an immutable event log.

docs.title: 3. What happens if a scanned medical invoice has poor image quality or low OCR confidence?
docs.text: The platform enforces a safety threshold (REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.75): - Any document with an overall confidence score below 75% or with active fraud flags is given a status of needs_review. - It will not trigger an automated purchase request. - It is placed in the review queue (GET /api/documents?status=needs_review), where hospital staff can view the original image in MinIO, correct the extracted fields, and approve the document. Approving emits a documents.reviewed event to proceed safely.

docs.title: 4. How does Open Policy Agent (OPA) decide the approval routing chain?
docs.text: Approval chains are dynamically constructed by evaluating three vectors in policies/opa/approval_rules.rego: 1. Total Spend: Small purchases (< ₹50,000) require only Department Manager sign-off; high-value purchases (> ₹2,000,000) require Department Manager, Finance Manager, and Procurement Director. 2. Department: Clinical departments (e.g., Cardiology, Oncology) require departmental head sign-off. 3. Real-time Vendor Risk Tier: High-risk vendors automatically trigger an extra compliance review step, regardless of spend amount.

docs.title: 5. How does the system handle cold-chain requirements for vaccines and biologics?
docs.text: Stock items can be marked with cold_chain: true: - When reserving stock, inventory_intelligence verifies that the warehouse location has active cold-chain compliance and that batch expiry dates are safely in the future. - The system prohibits splitting a cold-chain order across different incompatible storage batches. - If inventory is insufficient, the system records an atomic backorder hold and issues an alert to procurement.

docs.title: 6. Do I need to host OpenSign to test the digital contract e-signature flow?
docs.text: No. While contract_intelligence is equipped to send real HTTP requests to an active OpenSign instance (OPENSIGN_BASE_URL), it contains an internal mock envelope simulator: - If OPENSIGN_BASE_URL is unreachable or unset, the service generates a simulated signature envelope and dispatches the signed webhook callback internally. - This allows the entire demo flow — from purchase approval to contract generation and signed archive — to complete without spinning up a separate MongoDB/Parse-Server stack.

docs.title: 7. How are database migrations managed across microservices?
docs.text: MediSource AI follows a database-per-service model: - Each service contains an Alembic migration tree under services/<service>/alembic/. - On startup, each container invokes app/schema_bootstrap.py, which inspects the local database, automatically applies any pending Alembic revisions, or stamps the baseline for legacy databases. No manual migration commands are required during development.

docs.title: 8. How do I build and preview this MkDocs documentation site?
docs.text:
You can preview the documentation locally with hot-reloading: 

python -m mkdocs serve
Then visit http://localhost:8000.

To build the static HTML site for production deployment (e.g., GitHub Pages, S3, or Nginx): 

python -m mkdocs build
The compiled HTML and assets will be output to the site/ directory.

docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have the following installed on your system:

Tool Version Requirement Purpose Docker 24.0+ Container engine Docker Compose v2.20+ Multi-container orchestration Git 2.30+ Source code version control Python (Optional) 3.11+ Running local seed scripts or client SDKs RAM 8 GB minimum (16 GB recommended) Running OCR, Kafka, MLflow, and Postgres

docs.title: 1. Environment Configuration
docs.text:
Clone the repository and prepare your environment file:

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell) 
git clone https://github.com/maanvi21/fractal-major-proj.git
cd fractal-major-proj
cp .env.example .env

git clone https://github.com/maanvi21/fractal-major-proj.git
Set-Location fractal-major-proj
Copy-Item .env.example .env

docs.title: Optional LLM Acceleration (Groq)
docs.text:
Open .env in your text editor. By default, MediSource AI runs with zero external dependencies using rule-based and regex extractors.

To enable state-of-the-art LLM extraction and deep semantic fraud screening: 1. Obtain a free API key from Groq Console. 2. Set GROQ_API_KEY in your .env: 

GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_your_groq_api_key_here
GROQ_MODEL=llama3-70b-8192

docs.title: 2. One-Command Automated Deployment
docs.text:
MediSource AI provides automated deployment scripts that spin up 16 containerized services, await database health checks, create Kafka topics, and seed mock hospital data.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell) 
chmod +x scripts/deploy.sh
./scripts/deploy.sh

.\scripts\deploy.ps1

docs.title: What the deploy script does:
docs.text:
1. Validates and generates .env if missing.
  2. Executes docker compose up -d --build for all services and databases.
  3. Polls PostgreSQL, MinIO, and Kafka until health checks report healthy.
  4. Executes Alembic schema migrations across all 6 service databases (app/schema_bootstrap.py).
  5. Provisions 14 partitioned Kafka topics (documents.processed, approval.approved, etc.).
  6. Installs Python dependencies (requests, reportlab) and runs scripts/seed-data.py to seed sample hospitals, suppliers, invoices, and purchase requests.

docs.title: 3. Manual Deployment with Docker Compose
docs.text: If you prefer to start the containers manually step-by-step:

docs.title: Step 1: Build and Launch Containers
docs.text: docker compose up -d --build

docs.title: Step 2: Verify Container Health
docs.text: docker compose ps

docs.title: Step 3: Initialize Kafka Topics
docs.text:
# Linux / macOS
bash scripts/init-kafka-topics.sh

# Or directly through Docker Compose
docker compose exec -T kafka kafka-topics --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
    --create --if-not-exists --topic documents.processed --partitions 3 --replication-factor 1

docs.title: Step 4: Seed Demo Data
docs.text:
pip install requests reportlab
python scripts/seed-data.py

docs.title: 4. Port Map & Service Endpoints
docs.text:
Once deployed, the following endpoints and administrative dashboards will be available:

Service / Interface URL Credentials / Notes Unified Web Application http://localhost React + Bootstrap SPA via Nginx Gateway API Gateway http://localhost/api Single-origin proxy to all 7 microservices Temporal Web UI http://localhost:8088 Visual workflow tracking & approval SLAs MLflow Tracking UI http://localhost:5000 Risk model training runs, metrics & artifacts MinIO Console http://localhost:9001 Object storage for invoices & PDFs (minioadmin / minioadmin) Open Policy Agent (OPA) http://localhost:8181 Rego policy evaluation engine

docs.title: 5. Health Checks
docs.text:
Every service exposes a standardized /health endpoint to monitor operational status:

# Test API gateway health routing
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/documents
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/vendors
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/approvals
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/inventory
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/contracts
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/risk
curl -i http://localhost/api/health/notifications

Expected JSON response: 

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "service": "document_intelligence",
  "database": "connected"
}

docs.title: 6. Teardown & Reset
docs.text:
To stop all services: 

docker compose down

To stop all services and remove persistent volumes (Postgres, MinIO, Redis data): 

docker compose down -v

docs.title: User Guide & Workflows
docs.text: This guide covers real-world usage scenarios in MediSource AI, illustrating how hospital procurement officers, department managers, and compliance leads interact with the system.

docs.title: 1. Vendor Onboarding & Qualification
docs.text: Hospitals must rigorously verify pharmaceutical distributors and biomedical contractors prior to purchasing.

docs.title: Onboard a New Vendor via API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost/api/vendors \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-User-Role: procurement_director" \
  -d '{
    "legal_name": "Apex Medical Devices Pvt Ltd",
    "vendor_type": "equipment_supplier",
    "gst_number": "27AABCU9603R1ZX",
    "drug_license_number": "DL-MH-2024-88910",
    "drug_license_expiry": "2027-12-31",
    "fda_cdsco_registration_id": "CDSCO-MD-2024-0012",
    "contact_email": "orders@apexmed.com",
    "contact_phone": "+91-98200-11223"
  }'

docs.title: Automatic Validation Checks:
docs.text:
1. GSTIN Checksum: Regex & state code validation against Indian GST format.
  2. Drug License Expiry: Prevents onboarding vendors whose pharmaceutical or medical distribution licenses have lapsed.
  3. Watchlist Screening: Automatic matching against regulatory and sanctions databases.

docs.title: 2. Ingesting Invoices & Document Intelligence
docs.text: When a medical invoice or PO is received, it is ingested through the single-entry endpoint.

docs.title: Ingesting an Invoice
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost/api/documents/ingest \
  -H "X-User-Role: department_manager" \
  -F "file=@sample_invoice.pdf" \
  -F "source=upload"

docs.title: Ingestion Response:
docs.text:
{
  "document_id": "7f8b9912-349c-48be-8123-5e9213456789",
  "status": "extracted",
  "doc_type": "invoice",
  "vendor_id": "c19b2234-9210-44af-8899-712399123456",
  "overall_confidence": 0.94,
  "extraction_engine": "llm",
  "fraud_flag": false,
  "fraud_score": 0.05,
  "extracted_fields": {
    "invoice_number": "INV-2026-901",
    "invoice_date": "2026-10-15",
    "total_amount": 125000.0,
    "tax_amount": 15000.0,
    "line_items": [
      {
        "sku": "MED-STENT-01",
        "description": "Drug-Eluting Coronary Stent",
        "batch_number": "BT-2026-A1",
        "expiry_date": "2028-06-30",
        "quantity": 10,
        "unit_price": 11000.0
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Review Queue Handling
docs.text: If confidence drops below 0.75 (e.g. low-resolution scanned fax) or fraud checks fail: - Status is set to needs_review. - Document appears in the review queue: GET /api/documents?status=needs_review. - A human operator corrects or verifies fields via POST /api/documents/{id}/review. - Approving re-emits a documents.reviewed Kafka event to proceed down the pipeline.

docs.title: 3. Creating & Routing Procurement Approvals
docs.text: Once extracted, procurement requests are evaluated by Open Policy Agent (OPA).

docs.title: Initiating a Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost/api/approvals/requests \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-User-Role: department_manager" \
  -d '{
    "requested_by": "Dr. Sarah",
    "department": "Cardiology",
    "category": "consumables",
    "vendor_id": "c19b2234-9210-44af-8899-712399123456",
    "items": [
      {"sku": "MED-STENT-01", "quantity": 10, "unit_price": 11000.0}
    ],
    "total_value": 110000.0,
    "currency": "INR"
  }'

docs.title: Dynamic Step Chain Generated:
docs.text: Because total value exceeds ₹100,000, OPA configures a multi-tier chain: 1. Department Manager (Dr. Sarah) — Approval SLA: 24h 2. Finance Manager (Mark) — Spend and budget validation 3. Procurement Director (Arthur) — High-value contract execution sign-off

docs.title: Making an Approval Decision:
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost/api/approvals/requests/{request_id}/decide \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-User-Role: finance_manager" \
  -d '{
    "decision": "approved",
    "decision_note": "Budget verified against Q4 Cardiology allocations."
  }'

docs.title: 4. Inventory Reservation & Cold-Chain Guardrails
docs.text:
When a request is submitted, inventory_intelligence verifies stock and reserves units:

curl -X POST http://localhost/api/inventory/reserve \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-User-Role: department_manager" \
  -d '{
    "request_id": "a98c7654-2101-44af-9988-123456789abc",
    "sku": "MED-VAX-02",
    "quantity": 50
  }'

Cold-Chain Integrity Protection

If the requested SKU is marked cold_chain: true, the system: 1. Verifies that all units belong to a valid unexpired batch stored within temperature tolerances. 2. Enforces non-split reservations across incompatible batches. 3. If warehouse stock is insufficient, it immediately raises a backorder via inventory.backorder.

docs.title: 5. Contract Generation & Digital E-Signature
docs.text:
Upon final approval, contract_intelligence compiles an official agreement:

curl -X POST http://localhost/api/contracts/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-User-Role: procurement_director" \
  -d '{
    "template_type": "supply_agreement",
    "vendor_id": "c19b2234-9210-44af-8899-712399123456",
    "request_id": "a98c7654-2101-44af-9988-123456789abc",
    "effective_date": "2026-11-01",
    "expiry_date": "2027-10-31"
  }'

docs.title: Dispatching E-Signature:
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost/api/contracts/{contract_id}/send-for-signature \
  -H "X-User-Role: procurement_director"
The PDF is dispatched to OpenSign. When signed, the webhook updates status to signed and notifies the hospital legal archive.

docs.title: 6. Real-Time Vendor Risk & Anomaly Monitoring
docs.text:
Query real-time vendor risk profile and AI anomaly detection reasons:

curl -X GET http://localhost/api/risk/vendors/c19b2234-9210-44af-8899-712399123456 \
  -H "X-User-Role: finance_manager"

docs.title: Risk Response:
docs.text:
{
  "vendor_id": "c19b2234-9210-44af-8899-712399123456",
  "risk_band": "low",
  "overall_risk": 0.18,
  "dimensions": {
    "compliance_risk": 0.05,
    "fraud_risk": 0.02,
    "financial_risk": 0.22,
    "supplier_risk": 0.15,
    "spend_risk": 0.12,
    "operational_risk": 0.10
  },
  "anomaly_flag": false,
  "observation_count": 42,
  "is_cold_start": false
}
If anomaly_flag is true, details are returned under anomaly_reasons (e.g. ["sudden_spend_spike_3x", "delivery_delays_detected"]).
